maori_and_population_scope.volume_note: Māori population is excluded from tables in Parts I–X and separately reported in Appendix C. The Māori census was taken in February 1891, apart from the 5 April census night for the other tables.
maori_and_population_scope.interpretation: The Wellington Borough totals and male/female counts match exactly (31,021; 15,189; 15,832). The population table explicitly includes Chinese and half-castes in its total; the religion table’s exclusion is Māori only. Their responses are not separately cross-tabulated in this sample.

religion_sample.unit: Wellington Borough, same 1891 source unit in Table XVII and Table VII
religion_sample.selection: Purposive examples of common denominations and response-status categories; no exhaustive table extraction, percentages, or category sums.
religion_sample.not_selected: Bible Christians; Methodists—Others; Evangelists; Christadelphians; Unitarians; Society of Friends; Swedenborgians; Greek Church; Catholic Apostolic; Latter-day Saints/Mormons; Pagans; other table rows. Their omission from this packet is not zero.

methods_and_uncertainty.method: Transcribed exact rows from structured tables in official Stats NZ HTML. Compared totals and sex counts between paired population and religion tables at provincial-district and borough levels.
methods_and_uncertainty.variable: Published religious-denomination counts; not translated to Atlas identities, culture, primary affiliation, or beliefs beyond the table heading.
methods_and_uncertainty.precision: Integer headcounts of persons, males, and females; no interpolation or spatial allocation.
methods_and_uncertainty.uncertainty: The publication supplies no sampling errors or confidence intervals for these census counts. This review does not independently assess response coverage, classification practices, or exact historical boundary footprints. Matching table totals show denominator compatibility, not individual-row validation.
methods_and_uncertainty.temporal_scope: Single census night on 5 April 1891, not an interval. Historical unit labels retained as printed; no modern geographic equivalence inferred.
